summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with worsening low back pain and muscle spasms over two weeks, complicated by difficulty moving due to pain and recent noncompliance with lactulose. MRI showed degenerative disc disease at L5-S1 without nerve compression or cauda equina. Pain was managed with oxycodone, diazepam, tizanidine, and a lidocaine patch. Due to his history of hepatic encephalopathy, bowel regimen was intensified with lactulose, senna, and docusate to prevent constipation. He remained mentally clear throughout. No ascites was found on ultrasound. He was discharged home with a plan for outpatient physical therapy, follow-up in the chronic pain clinic, and clear instructions to avoid sedating medications if confusion develops.
